subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `openclaw models status --probe --all` as the canonical configured-model health check, or fold this need into fallback-chain testing or staged model-migration UX instead?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this adds a new live CLI probe mode over provider credentials and overlaps two other model diagnostics workflows, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract alone.

options.title: Add Status Probe All
options.body: Add `--probe --all` to `models status`, preserve default one-model-per-provider probing, and document cost/rate-limit/output behavior for all configured models.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback Testing
options.body: Make the fallback-chain testing request own configured fallback verification and keep `models status --probe` as provider/auth-profile diagnostics.

options.title: Defer To Migration UX
options.body: Treat model validation as one step of a staged model migration workflow and avoid a new standalone status flag until that larger flow is scoped.

recommendation.title: Add Status Probe All
recommendation.body: Add `--probe --all` to `models status`, preserve default one-model-per-provider probing, and document cost/rate-limit/output behavior for all configured models.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the live auth probe surface and has already provided product-scoping guidance in this diagnostics cluster.
